title: NHOS Oracle Matrix Search Engine™: A Local Hybrid Retrieval, Ontology-Aware, and Federated Sync Architecture for Personal Health Knowledge Technical Research White Paper — Architecture, Methodology & Validation Framework
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: NHOS Oracle Matrix Search Engine™: A Local Hybrid Retrieval, Ontology-Aware, and Federated Sync Architecture for Personal Health Knowledge Technical Research White Paper — Architecture, Methodology & Validation Framework Overview This white paper documents NHOS Oracle Matrix Search Engine™ v16.0.0, an implemented local-first health-information retrieval and contextual discovery system developed within the NHOS Intelligence Matrix Engine™ (NIME™) research program. The system composes hybrid lexical/fuzzy retrieval, multi-concept Matrix processing, on-device NLP normalization, concept-graph-assisted expansion, isotonic confidence calibration, deployment-state transparency, cross-tab federated synchronization, and browser-native voice input into a single architecture for personal health knowledge discovery. The paper is the first public publication documenting the complete v6.3 → v16.0.0 evolution in a single revision. It supersedes five previously unpublished internal drafts (v1.0–v1.4) and reconciles the historical record across the v6.3 baseline, the v7.x Scientific/Modular lineage, and the v8.x NLP/Localization/Deployment-State lineage. What This Paper Documents Part I — Research Foundation: Problem definition, research gap, 20 research questions (RQ1–RQ20), 8 research objectives, scope and delimitations, and architectural positioning within NIME™. Part II — Oracle Architecture & Retrieval: Ten-layer system architecture, knowledge aggregation pipeline, index construction, query processing pipeline, normalization/tokenization/query planning, exact and fuzzy matching, Porter stemmer, concept ontology, category weighting, synonym expansion, ontology expansion, type-specific boosting, ranking and scoring, algorithmic confidence, waterfall explanation, isotonic calibration, and the NHOS Matrix Engine. Part III — Matrix & Recommendation Intelligence: Multi-concept query parsing, concept extraction, Matrix matching, matched-concept tracking, Matrix confidence/coverage, Matrix-vs-Hybrid comparison, graph traversal, local interaction history, session context, recommendation generation pipeline, deterministic candidate selection, intelligence layer (herb actions, symptom clusters, evidence inference), and recommendation influence. Part IV — Application/Interaction Architecture: Local search analytics, configuration panel, search history panel, autocomplete, voice search pipeline, voice-query correction, filtering/sorting/facets/clustering, Clinical Mode and v16 clinical scoring boosts, knowledge discovery routing, saved knowledge, export architecture (CSV/PDF/JSON/XML/DOCX/FHIR R4), sharing, and local-first architecture. Part V — Local-First Infrastructure: Local persistence, offline architecture, SHA-256 corpus integrity verification, privacy model, security boundaries, data lifecycle, implementation status, and local telemetry. Part VI — Evidence Discipline & Safety: Explicit non-claims, known technical limitations, failure modes, safety boundaries, and the distinction between implementation and empirical validation. Part VII — Scientific Evaluation: Evaluation framework, benchmark dataset design, human relevance judgment protocol, precision/recall, MRR/nDCG, confidence calibration, Matrix Engine evaluation, ablation studies, baseline comparisons, recommendation evaluation, privacy/network evaluation, offline evaluation, performance evaluation, scalability evaluation, and error analysis. Part VIII — Research Program: Reproducibility artifact contract, reproducibility protocol, embedded test suite (17 assertions), research roadmap, Q4 2026–Q2 2027 validation program, 23 research contributions, relationship to NIME™, future research, explainable retrieval, scientific interpretation, and conclusion. Appendices A–N: Core terminology, hybrid retrieval pipeline, Matrix Engine pipeline, proposed validation matrix, evidence classification, publication integrity statement, research position, implementation status matrices, benchmark specification template, validation record template, v6.3 → v16.0.0 changelog, Zenodo deposit metadata, and version history summary. Key Architectural Subsystems (v16.0.0) Subsystem Description Hybrid Retrieval Exact/content, title/excerpt, token-level, Levenshtein fuzzy (≤2), category weighting, type-specific boosting NHOS Matrix Engine Delimiter-based multi-concept parsing (5 delimiter classes), concept-by-concept matching, matched-concept tracking, coverage-based confidence NLP Normalization Layer Porter stemmer, ~40-entry curated synonym map, Levenshtein-based voice-query correction Concept Ontology 37-concept starter graph across 8 branches, graph-distance ranking boost (8 × 0.5^(d/halfLife)), regex-based relation extraction Query Planner Negation parsing, type-hint extraction, comparative operators, temporal markers Session Context 10 recent queries / 20 selections, JSON export/import Facets & Clustering Type/Category/Evidence refinement, TF-IDF k-means (k=5, hash-seeded centroids) Waterfall Explanation Per-category score contribution bars Vector Projection 256-dim hash-based (opt-in), L2-normalized, cosine similarity Extensibility Custom scorers, plugin system (5 hooks), query rewrites, local telemetry Isotonic Calibration Pool-adjacent-violators regression, opt-in, requires ≥30 labeled samples Federated Sync Five-source boot cascade (parent → localStorage → BroadcastChannel → server → embedded), CRDT primitives (Lamport, G-Set, LWW-Register), AES-GCM + PBKDF2 encrypted sync, cross-tab coordination, federation protocol Deployment-State Reporting Sync-state indicator (standalone / syncing / synchronized / synced-with-peers) Internationalization 7 languages (en, es, fr, de, it, pt, nl), configurable fallback chain, per-language coverage reporting Discoverability Static structured-data metadata (6 JSON-LD blocks), hreflang alternates, PWA manifest — no runtime telemetry Evidence Status NHOS Oracle Matrix Search Engine™ is an implemented research system. This paper documents its architecture, retrieval methodology, implemented capabilities, and proposed evaluation framework. Implementation status should not be interpreted as empirical validation. The paper intentionally does not claim: Superior retrieval performance Superior ranking quality Clinical effectiveness or diagnostic accuracy Recommendation effectiveness Calibrated confidence (except where explicitly fitted and evaluated) Reduced health-information errors or improved health outcomes Superiority to semantic/vector retrieval, BM25, or TF-IDF Privacy or security superiority Speech-recognition accuracy superiority Stemmer, synonym-coverage, ontology-coverage, or clustering-quality superiority Cross-tab sync reliability under adversarial conditions Measurably improved discoverability from the SEO block Statistically significant user benefit These are research hypotheses or validation targets scheduled for Q4 2026 – Q2 2027. Reproducibility A reproducible run of Oracle must record, at minimum: Engine version, build, schema version, corpus version Confidence method, routing triggers i18n language and fallback chain Stemming, synonym expansion, voice correction status Ontology loaded, concept count, coverage Vector projection active, vector count Clustering enabled Custom scorer count, plugin count Calibration blocks Item count Parent-sync status, sync state, sync source Last routing path Deterministic recommendations Voice supported Build type The canonical capture method is NHOSOracleHybridSearch.getStats(), which returns a plain JSON-serializable object independent of DOM state. Embedded test suite: NHOSOracleHybridSearch.runTests() executes 17 pure-function assertions; the shipped v16.0.0 build reports 17/17 passed. Companion Artifacts JAMIA Pilot Evaluation Package — 30-item curated corpus, 120-query benchmark spanning ten query categories, in-browser evaluation script, and human relevance-judgment template. Submitted for review at the Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association; results are not reported in this document. tools.html Corpus Publisher — Companion script that broadcasts NHOS host databases to any Oracle instance on the same origin. Structured-Data Metadata Block — Static metadata for search-engine discoverability; no runtime telemetry. Software Availability Public implementation: https://nhos.health/oracle/ Engine: NHOS Oracle Matrix Search Engine v16.0.0 Entry point (single-file): oracle_v16.html, self-contained Entry point (modular, strict CSP): oracle_v16.html + oracle.css + oracle.js No server, no build step, no network access required for core retrieval Runtime provenance: Call NHOSOracleHybridSearch.getStats() in the browser console Regression harness: Call NHOSOracleHybridSearch.runTests() Verification: scripts/verify-hashes.sh verifies vendor and corpus integrity Standalone sync: Auto-synchronizes from /oracle/data/corpus.json, from localStorage, or from any open tools.html tab on the same origin License Paper text: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0) Software: No license is asserted in the paper; the software deposit carries its own license.
